newsitem.title: THAILAND: No Thai central bank comment on baht intervention.
newsitem.headline: No Thai central bank comment on baht intervention.

text.p: Thailand's central bank officials were unavailable for comment on reports the bank had intervened in the Singapore foreign exchange market to defend the sliding baht.
A public relations officer at the Bank of Thailand (BOT) declined to comment on the reported intervention or the status of the baht.
The baht fell sharply early on Tuesday after offshore investors sold the currency heavily for the rising dollar.
The decline came on the back of an earlier fall on Monday afternoon.
Dealers said the BOT might have sold up to $500 million in dollars to defend the sliding baht.

They said heavy baht sales were made by some banks and investors to buy dollars for year-end book closings and position squaring. Speculators jumped on the bandwagon and also sold to see how far the BOT would defend the currency.
At 0520 GMT the baht was trading at 25.607-25.612 to the dollar after ranging at a day's high-low of 25.612 to 25.595.
